content: Norethindrone is a progestin-only oral contraceptive, commonly referred to as the mini-pill. It works primarily by inhibiting the release of gonadotropins from the pituitary gland, thereby preventing follicular maturation and ovulation. Additionally, it stimulates the growth of mammary tissues. Unlike combination oral contraceptives, it does not contain estrogen, making it a suitable option for women who cannot tolerate estrogen-containing medications. The bioavailability of norethindrone is approximately 64%, with peak plasma concentrations occurring within 1 to 2 hours after administration. Its volume of distribution (Vd) is 4 L/kg, and it is approximately 61% protein-bound in plasma. The drug undergoes hepatic metabolism, resulting in inactive sulfate and glucuronide metabolites. Its elimination half-life ranges from 4 to 13 hours, and it is excreted primarily through urine (33-81%) and feces (35-43%). This medication is less effective than combination hormonal contraceptives (which contain both estrogen and progestin) because it does not consistently suppress ovulation. However, it is more effective than barrier methods such as condoms, cervical caps, or diaphragms. It is typically prescribed for women who cannot use estrogen-containing contraceptives. Instructions for Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and with each refill. This leaflet contains critical information about when to take the pills and what to do if a dose is missed. Take the medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. To minimize stomach upset or nausea, it may be taken after an evening meal or at bedtime. Alternatively, you may choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. It is recommended to start taking the medication on the first day of your menstrual period. Continue taking one tablet daily without interruption. After finishing the last tablet in a pack, begin a new pack the following day without any break or use of reminder tablets (placebo pills). Be aware that your menstrual periods may become irregular, heavier, lighter, or you may experience spotting between periods. Missing pills, starting a new pack late, or taking the pill at inconsistent times increases the likelihood of pregnancy. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on switching from other forms of hormonal birth control (e.g., patches or other oral contraceptives) to this product. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, and weight gain. Vaginal spotting or irregular/missed periods may also occur. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. Precautions: Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to norethindrone, other progestins, or any inactive ingredients in the product. These inactive ingredients may cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause melasma (blotchy, dark areas on the skin, particularly the face). Sunlight can exacerbate this effect, so limit sun exposure and avoid tanning booths or sunlamps. Norethindrone should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Inform your doctor about all medications you are taking, as certain drugs (e.g., rifamycins, griseofulvin, modafinil, ritonavir) may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control, increasing the risk of pregnancy. Discuss the need for backup contraception methods, such as condoms or spermicides, when starting new medications. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of norethindrone or increase the risk of side effects. Maintain a list of all prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products you use, and share it with your healthcare provider. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., sex hormone-binding globulin, thyroid function tests), potentially causing inaccurate results. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless directed to do so. Important Notes: Regular physical exams, including blood pressure checks, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, are recommended while using this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examination of your breasts and report any lumps immediately. This summary does not contain all possible information about norethindrone. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details tailored to your specific health needs.
